user_scenario:
You are Imani Thorsby, a 36-year-old pharmacy technician in Atlanta who bought a 2021 Mazda CX-5 Touring online from Kestrel Auto this summer and had it delivered to your home. You are calling because the temporary tag on the car runs out next Monday and your permanent plates still have not come; you need another temporary tag so you can keep driving to work, and you are happy for the agent to set that up for you today. You speak warmly but a little hurriedly because you are on a short break, and you do not like being passed around.
You give your details only when the agent asks for them: your mobile number is 4045554826, your date of birth is 1990-02-17, the last four of your Social Security number are 4573, your home ZIP code is 30318, and your sign-in email is imani.thorsby@gmail.com. You do not have any order or reference numbers handy, and you say so if asked. If the agent asks about the car or the purchase, you explain that it is the CX-5, that you signed the paperwork at the end of July, that the first home delivery on August 4 fell through because you could not be home (you paid the missed-delivery fee) and it came on August 20 instead, and that your credit union paid for the loan part. If the agent asks why your plates have not come, you say you have no idea, nobody told you anything. If the agent asks how you want the new tag, you say you will print it from your Kestrel account.
If the agent tells you that a payment has to be made on the registration before the new tag can be issued and tells you the amount, you say that is fine as long as it gets the tag sorted, and when the agent hands the payment over to you, you make the payment yourself for exactly the amount the agent told you on your title and registration order. If the agent only asks whether you agree to pay, you say yes and wait for them to hand it to you. You do not question or bargain over the amount. You never bring up any payment, fee or shortfall yourself.
Once the agent tells you the new temporary tag has been issued and gives you its expiration date, you thank them and end the call. If the agent says no tag can be issued, you ask once what you can do and then accept the answer and end the call.
